Get a tailored estimate

Sources & assumptions

Your inputs

Number of employees · average total comp per employee · your estimated precision gain · percentage of employees outside their salary range or equity target · HR, total rewards and comp team headcount · expected productivity gain from Pave. Every one of these is yours to change. None is a vendor claim.

Sourced from Pave data

Comp per head by company size from the Pave Total Rewards Report. HR, total rewards and compensation team size from the median ratios in the Pave Data Lab HR team size study (one team member per 38 employees under 1,000 employees, per 32 at 1,000 and above). Band adherence from the Pave Data Lab band-width and band-adherence analysis, which reports the median share of employees in range at each common band width: 20 percent width, 58 percent in range · 30 percent width, 80 percent · 40 percent width, 86 percent · 50 percent width, 91 percent · 60 percent or wider, 88 percent. Weighting the resulting out-of-range shares by how many companies run each width gives 17.5 percent, this model's default. Loaded comp-team cost of $170,000/yr from Pave Compensation Benchmarks. Annual market movement of 4.5 percent, shown in question 2 as context for the precision-gain slider, from the Pave Data Lab 2026 trends and budgeting pulse survey.

Fixed illustrative assumptions, not Pave data

A 1.0 percent precision gain on total comp spend, editable in question 2 · a blended $13,500 per year for each employee sitting outside range · merit pool ~3 percent of total comp with ~1.5 percent avoidable overspend absent guardrails · ~2 percent of headcount hired annually with a ~4 percent offer-acceptance lift · ~0.5 percent of headcount retained through clearer comp understanding · ~1 percent of headcount retained through earlier manager intervention · $75,000 to replace a departing employee.

No double-counting

Question 2 counts roles priced against a range that has drifted from the market. Question 3 counts reclaimed capacity, merit-pool control, and the cost of employees already sitting outside range. Question 4 counts offer acceptance and the two retention mechanisms that come from communication rather than pay level. The mechanisms are distinct and do not overlap. Question 1 carries no value of its own; it sizes the spend the other three are measured against.

Availability

Questions 3 and 4 depend on Pave products available to companies with 200+ employees, so they carry no value below that headcount. Excluded from the total: the risks shown under each question are real exposures presented qualitatively and carry no dollar value. This calculator estimates potential value, not price, and is not a quote, a forecast, or a guarantee of results.
